title: NVIDIA adds permanent export oversight
caption: NVIDIA added a standing export oversight committee, began engaging counsel and announced a compliance officer search as the independent investigation continued.

title: Marvell can build around a customer’s chip design
caption: Marvell can supply chiplets, IP, packaging and production expertise around the hyperscaler’s own compute design.

title: Huang returned as CEO. Jones stayed chair.
caption: The filing puts Huang back as CEO on 22 November, and NVIDIA confirmed that Jones stayed chair and Kress stayed CFO.

title: NVIDIA said its board inquiry would continue
caption: NVIDIA said its board inquiry and cooperation with government inquiries would continue after Huang returned.

title: Water reuse can coexist with water stress
caption: Samsung reported substantial reuse at its Korean semiconductor sites and still classified those sites as facing medium-high water stress.

title: Cloud commitments differ from product sales
caption: NVIDIA books product revenue when the customer takes control, and it assesses closely related agreements together.

title: An efficiency scenario can’t measure AI rebound
caption: The IEA scenario holds demand constant, so it cannot measure how much extra AI use would offset energy savings.

title: Packaging expansion leaves Taiwan exposure
caption: Amkor is expanding in Arizona and South Korea, while Vera Rubin still uses TSMC packaging and SPIL is expanding in Taiwan.

title: US licensing was active as new rules were discussed
caption: NVIDIA’s August filing describes actual H200 licences alongside a planned AI Diffusion rule replacement and a cloud-access bill under consideration.

title: GPU export curbs can spill into networking
caption: NVIDIA quantified unshipped H20 sales and separately warned that GPU curbs could also weaken demand for its networking equipment.

title: Rivals target both training and inference
caption: AWS and Google offer chips for both training and inference, while Intel targets demanding model workloads and Meta built its own recommendation silicon.

title: Supply can falter without conflict
caption: NVIDIA relies on foundries and independent contractors, and says it has previously experienced lead times longer than twelve months.

title: ESG risk extends beyond emissions
caption: NVIDIA reported supplier labour violations and separately warned that legal, social and ethical issues could slow AI adoption.

title: New GPUs can erode the value of older ones
caption: Faster new chips can pressure returns on older GPUs, and NVIDIA says customers can generally change or delay purchase commitments.

title: Kress brought prior CFO experience
caption: Kress had divisional CFO roles at Microsoft and Cisco before joining NVIDIA as CFO, and her CEO appointment was interim.

title: The estimated equity risk premium varies
caption: The same method gave different historical estimates, so the premium is a model input and cannot guarantee what investors earn.

title: Morningstar and our DCF use different margins
caption: Morningstar forecasts gross margin, while our DCF uses a free-cash-flow margin of 45.25%, so the percentages measure different things.

title: UK chip export controls depend on the item and use
caption: The UK arms embargo covers certain military items, and separate controls can require a licence depending on the item and its end use.

title: A strong chip forecast leaves room for a downturn
caption: SIA forecast industry sales above $1.5 trillion, but NVIDIA can still face a downturn.

title: External use of CDP scores needs written consent
caption: CDP says to obtain written consent for any use outside internal, non-commercial use, including for a pitch shared externally.

title: BIS puts listed entities under tighter chip controls
caption: BIS tightened controls on seven listed entities over diversion risk, and the rule itself makes no finding of wrongdoing by NVIDIA.

title: Gaming fell while Data Center grew
caption: NVIDIA Gaming revenue fell in FY23 while Data Center grew, so it matters which markets are exposed when demand weakens.

title: Women’s share of NVIDIA’s board fell
caption: NVIDIA reports a smaller share of women on its board in FY26 than in FY25, even as women’s representation in its workforce rose.

title: Data centres could take a larger share of U.S. power
caption: Berkeley Lab’s projection spans 6.7% to 12% of U.S. electricity use in 2028 across all data centres.

title: The largest direct buyer’s share fell year over year
caption: The biggest disclosed direct customer took a smaller share than a year earlier, and some indirect customers still account for material demand.

title: Microsoft has substantial future data-centre commitments
caption: Microsoft’s construction commitments and future leases show the scale of its infrastructure plans, while its annual GPU budget remains undisclosed in these figures.

title: Grid-based emissions rose as market-based emissions fell
caption: NVIDIA’s local-grid measure rose over the period, while its procurement-based measure fell sharply.

title: NVIDIA’s free cash flow swings from quarter to quarter
caption: NVIDIA’s free cash flow dropped sharply in the second quarter of FY27 and rebounded the following quarter.

title: The IEA projects rising data-centre emissions
caption: The IEA projects rising electricity-related emissions from data centres in both scenarios shown.

title: Nuclear deals take years to deliver power
caption: The original nuclear plans targeted later delivery, and the IEA still expects coal and gas to supply a large share of added data-centre electricity.

title: NVIDIA’s workforce grew sharply
caption: Bloomberg records a sharp increase in NVIDIA’s workforce between these fiscal year-ends.

title: NVIDIA disclosed $25bn in ecosystem equity commitments
caption: NVIDIA reported a large ecosystem equity portfolio and further commitments, while leaving the amount attributable to customers unquantified.

title: Marvell’s data-centre sales grew
caption: Marvell’s broader data-centre revenue grew year on year, and the release leaves custom-chip sales undisclosed.

title: H20 restrictions triggered charges and blocked shipments
caption: The booked inventory charge, blocked shipments and forecast losses measure different things, leaving the final net cost unresolved.

title: NVIDIA sharply increased R&D spending
caption: NVIDIA’s reported research and development expense rose sharply from the same quarter a year earlier.

title: AI clouds, industrial and enterprise grew faster
caption: Both groups grew, and the combined AI cloud, industrial and enterprise category grew faster than hyperscalers.

title: Gas and coal still matter for data-centre growth
caption: In the IEA base case, gas and coal meet more than 40% of the extra electricity data centres need globally through 2030.

title: Software and GPUs both improved efficiency
caption: In one translation workload, caching, GPU acceleration and lower precision each improved efficiency as researchers changed the system.

title: How operating cash became free cash flow
caption: NVIDIA deducts equipment and intangible purchases and related principal payments from operating cash flow to calculate free cash flow.

title: Broadcom offers several Ethernet port speeds
caption: Broadcom offers different combinations of port speed and port count, and comparing energy use still requires a matched workload test.

title: Black and Hispanic workforce shares changed little
caption: The reported shares for Black and Hispanic or Latino employees changed little over the three fiscal years shown.

title: Data centres could take a larger share of global power
caption: The IEA estimates about one and a half percent of world electricity in 2024 and projects just under three percent in its 2030 base case.

title: Turnover kept rising for Hispanic or Latino US staff
caption: Turnover kept rising among Hispanic or Latino US staff, while the rate for Black or African American US staff eased slightly in FY26.

title: Samsung reports water use at water-stressed sites
caption: Samsung reports how much its device division withdrew and consumed at sites facing high or worse baseline water stress.

title: NVIDIA reported no H20 sales to China-based buyers
caption: After the licensing requirement, NVIDIA reported no second-quarter H20 sales to China-based customers and about $650 million in unrestricted sales to one customer outside China.

title: AWS reports higher throughput for Trainium3
caption: AWS reports more memory bandwidth and up to twice the rated compute throughput for Trainium3, with workload costs and energy still to be measured.

title: NVIDIA’s direct emissions rose each year
caption: NVIDIA’s direct emissions rose in each year shown, while electricity and supply-chain emissions sit in separate scopes.

title: AI adoption could swing data-centre power demand
caption: The IEA’s high-efficiency case is about 970 TWh in 2035, while faster adoption and deployment take its lift-off case above 1,700 TWh.

title: NVIDIA disclosed a maximum loss on some AI stakes
caption: NVIDIA’s August filing puts maximum loss exposure on certain infrastructure-financier investments at $4.7 billion, including carrying values and future commitments.

title: NVIDIA’s reporting change breaks the water trend
caption: NVIDIA changed how it collects water data in FY26, so the reported withdrawal and consumption figures cannot establish a year-on-year trend.

title: Bristol reports low power overhead at Isambard-AI
caption: Bristol reports a power usage effectiveness of about 1.08 for Isambard-AI versus around 2.0 for a typical air-cooled supercomputer, with the averaging period unspecified.

title: Employees put NVIDIA near the top of the Fortune list
caption: NVIDIA placed sixth on the 2026 Fortune workplace list, which drew on nearly 640,000 employee responses across eligible employers.

title: Samsung’s device sites discharged most water they withdrew
caption: Samsung’s device division discharged most of the water it withdrew, while it reported 3,512 thousand tonnes as consumed.

title: Automotive sales edged higher in FY26
caption: Automotive reached $604 million in the final quarter before NVIDIA began grouping it with other businesses in Edge Computing.

title: Azure passed a new revenue milestone
caption: Microsoft says Azure surpassed $75 billion and then $100 billion in successive fiscal years across AI and other workloads.

title: NVIDIA backs some cloud partners’ leases
caption: NVIDIA reported $3.5 billion in maximum gross exposure on these guarantees and $712 million in partner escrow to cushion potential losses.

title: Three direct buyers each drove a large share of sales
caption: The three biggest direct customers each represented a substantial slice of first-half revenue, and direct buyers can serve multiple end customers.

title: UK public AI compute uses several suppliers
caption: Isambard-AI gives NVIDIA a foothold in UK public compute, while Cambridge’s Dawn and Zenith show demand reaches other suppliers too.

title: Samsung withdrew more water each year
caption: Samsung’s group-wide withdrawals rose across the three years, and these figures cannot tell us how much water went into making NVIDIA products.

title: Analysts disagree far more about FY28 revenue
caption: The later-year revenue estimates are spread much farther apart, so the consensus average hides a wide range of views.

title: NVIDIA’s remaining buyback authority rose
caption: NVIDIA had more room to buy back shares after the September approval, and any future purchases remain discretionary.

title: NVIDIA still uses fuel alongside renewable electricity
caption: NVIDIA reported fully renewable electricity in its operations and separately disclosed more fuel use in the latest year.

title: Bristol attributes lower emissions to its modular build
caption: Bristol estimates its modular build cut construction emissions by about 72% compared with traditional methods, while the full lifecycle footprint remains unverified.

title: NVIDIA’s stock compensation expense rose
caption: NVIDIA recorded higher stock-based compensation across the same nine months, and diluted share counts are the separate measure to check for net dilution.

title: Azure and other cloud services grew faster by June
caption: Microsoft reported faster growth across Azure and other cloud services by June, covering AI and other workloads.

title: NVIDIA’s U.S. workplace incident rate fell
caption: NVIDIA’s U.S. recordable incident rate fell each year across the reported period.

title: Data-centre electricity use was already growing fast
caption: The IEA estimates global data-centre electricity use was already growing about 12% a year before the forecast period.

title: NVIDIA’s largest direct buyer took a bigger share
caption: The biggest disclosed direct buyer rose from 12% of annual sales in FY25 to 22% in FY26.

title: NVIDIA’s renewable figure covers its own operations
caption: NVIDIA reports fully renewable electricity for its own operations, while Greenpeace estimates roughly a quarter for an East Asian supplier sample.

title: Samsung withdrew and discharged more water
caption: Samsung’s group reported higher withdrawal and wastewater discharge in 2025 than in 2023, across both semiconductor and device operations.

title: Cloud systems gained share in MLPerf training
caption: Cloud-based systems made up more of the latest MLPerf Training round, a measure of who entered the benchmark.

title: Hyperscalers were just over half of sales
caption: Hyperscalers accounted for just over half of revenue, while AI clouds, industrial and enterprise made up another substantial share.

title: Google consumed most of the water it withdrew
caption: Google says it consumed most of the water its data centres withdrew, counting consumption as the water it withdrew minus the water it returned.

title: NVIDIA claims lower inference energy for Blackwell
caption: NVIDIA claims up to a 25-fold reduction in inference energy in this comparison, while total electricity demand also depends on how much AI people use.

title: Data Center networking sales rose quarter on quarter
caption: Under the old reporting split, Data Center networking grew 35% from the previous quarter and 199% from the same quarter a year earlier.

title: Microsoft signed a long-term nuclear power deal
caption: The agreement commits Microsoft to buy power over 20 years and supports a planned reactor restart.

title: AMD lists more memory per chip than AWS
caption: AMD lists more memory per accelerator in this comparison, while throughput and cost need a workload benchmark.

title: Adjustments did not lift NVIDIA’s earnings per share
caption: NVIDIA reported $2.70 per diluted share under GAAP and $2.68 after its adjustments.

title: US licences led to few H200 sales in China
caption: Licensed H200 shipments were under 1% of Data Center revenue that quarter, and NVIDIA had already booked an inventory and purchase-obligation charge.

title: UK projects can apply for public GPU time
caption: The UK offers up to 20,000 GPU hours through Rapid Access and up to 10,000 through Gateway.

title: Bristol’s cooling claim covers one part of the site
caption: Bristol says the system can cut cooling power by up to 90%, and annual facility electricity savings would require a separate measurement.

title: NVIDIA trades near TSMC on EV/EBITDA
caption: On this trailing EBITDA measure, NVIDIA was valued near TSMC and below Broadcom and AMD.

title: Text prompts use energy beyond the AI chip
caption: Google measured 0.24 watt-hours for its median text prompt, of which 0.14 watt-hours came from the active AI accelerator.

title: Smelters face a deadline to fix audit findings
caption: Smelters and refiners in the extended corrective action programme have 12 months from enrolment to close findings before a final warning and removal.

title: Inventory rose while orders could still change
caption: NVIDIA carried more inventory in October, while customers could generally change or cancel purchase commitments at short notice.

title: NVIDIA targets more chip testing in early 2027
caption: NVIDIA is targeting high-volume chip testing in Singapore in February 2027 and at KYEC’s US facilities in April 2027.

title: AI Enterprise offers a trial and paid licences
caption: The 90-day production trial shows how customers can try AI Enterprise, and NVIDIA lists paid licences without separately disclosing sales.

title: Morningstar kept its lower value after reinstatement
caption: Morningstar cut fair value from $310 to $250 per share and kept the lower estimate after Huang returned.

title: Google has geothermal power on the grid
caption: Google reported geothermal power flowing to its local Nevada grid, while its first Kairos reactor date was an original project target.

title: Google cut energy per Gemini text prompt
caption: Google reported lower energy and emissions per median Gemini text prompt, while total impact still depends on usage.

title: Data Center leads AMD’s sales
caption: Data Center was AMD’s largest segment, and its sales included both EPYC CPUs and Instinct accelerators.

title: AI is a major part of Broadcom’s chip sales
caption: Broadcom’s reported AI semiconductor sales sit inside its chip segment and include networking as well as custom accelerators.

title: Professional Visualization sales climbed
caption: Professional Visualization rose from $509 million to about $1.3 billion during FY26 before NVIDIA grouped it into Edge Computing.

title: NVIDIA expects operating costs to rise
caption: NVIDIA guided to roughly $11 billion in operating expenses, with an extra week and transition costs in that forecast.

title: NVIDIA raised its quarterly dividend
caption: NVIDIA raised the quarterly dividend from one cent to twenty-five cents per share and kept that rate for the declared December payment.

title: NVIDIA has the lowest trailing P/E in this group
caption: On the November Stock Analysis snapshot, NVIDIA had the lowest trailing earnings multiple among these four chip companies.

title: The US overnight rate rose into October
caption: The monthly US overnight rate rose from August to October, while the rate we use to discount NVIDIA’s cash flows also reflects equity risk.

title: Supplier fixes still need worker-level proof
caption: NVIDIA reports working with suppliers on corrective plans, and we would ask affected workers to confirm that the fixes reached them.

title: Google estimates cooling water from energy
caption: Google combined the energy used to serve a median Gemini text prompt with its fleet-average water intensity to estimate direct cooling water.

title: The emissions total leaves out product use
caption: NVIDIA’s FY26 number leaves out product-use emissions, which the GHG Protocol measures over the expected lifetime of relevant products sold that year.

title: New substrate capacity ramps into 2028
caption: NVIDIA announced existing South Korean substrate capacity alongside planned ramps in Taiwan and Japan.

title: Software licences and support book at different times
caption: NVIDIA described recognising licences upfront and support over time, while its reported contract balance covers multiple offerings.

title: PwC’s tenure outlasts any lead partner
caption: PwC has audited NVIDIA since 2004, and NVIDIA’s proxy limits the lead partner to five consecutive years.

title: Trainium savings depend on the comparison
caption: AWS advertises up to 50% savings on Trn1, while one customer reported 20% in an AWS testimonial with its own comparator.

title: Accelerated-server electricity use could grow faster
caption: In the IEA’s base case, electricity use grows 30% a year for accelerated servers and 9% for conventional servers.

title: Marketable equities now exceed cash
caption: By October, NVIDIA held more in marketable equities than in cash and cash equivalents, and those investments carry market price risk.

title: Use NVIDIA’s reported free cash flow
caption: For FY26, cite NVIDIA’s $96,575 million in free cash flow, which deducts $101 million in principal payments.

title: The U.S. lost-time case rate stayed flat
caption: NVIDIA’s U.S. recordable incident rate fell from 0.11 to 0.07 per 200,000 labor hours, while its lost-time case rate stayed at 0.01.

title: Microsoft’s cloud gross margin fell
caption: Microsoft reported that cloud gross margin fell from 71% to 66% across these fiscal years and cited AI investment and usage among the drivers.

title: NVIDIA reports pay ratios close to parity
caption: NVIDIA reports global pay of 99.5 to 100 for women versus men, and its reported U.S. comparisons by race and ethnicity also sit close to parity.

title: Edge Computing sales climbed each quarter
caption: Edge Computing sales rose from $6.4 billion to $8.2 billion over the first three quarters, and the platform covers much more than Gaming.

title: Cooling capacity alone tells us little about water
caption: Ecolab’s 3-megawatt rating describes the equipment, and proving water savings requires comparable whole-site measurements.

title: Amkor plans more packaging capacity
caption: NVIDIA’s nearly $3 billion of Amkor agreements support more packaging capacity, while Rubin still relies on TSMC.

title: Stargate UAE is one part of a larger campus
caption: The first planned phase sits within Stargate UAE, which itself sits within the wider campus, and G42 gave no value for NVIDIA’s supply contract.

title: Microsoft’s commercial backlog held steady
caption: Microsoft’s commercial backlog was nearly flat from June to September, and the total spans its commercial business.

title: AMD guided to higher company-wide sales
caption: AMD reported $13.4 billion in third-quarter sales and guided to about $17 billion for the fourth quarter across the whole company.
